autopsy.role: Requirements, full-stack development, plans, payment approach, documentation and launch

decisions.title: Scope and audience
decisions.context: A freelance client wanted a stock screener: a personalised utility for the client, and a product for investment enthusiasts. Building it also meant learning AI and real-time screening of public market data.
decisions.decision: Started with a prototype, then ran about 12 iterations across the frontend, backend, authentication and security. Developed with Lovable and added database indexes for performance, without a caching layer.
decisions.reason: Iterating in small steps let me turn stakeholder requirements into working features and fix problems as they surfaced.
decisions.result: A customisable screener covering 5,300+ NSE and BSE stocks, with live prices, watchlists, portfolio tracking and real-time analysis. I aim to open-source it.
decisions.lesson: Working directly with the client taught me to think like a forward-deployed engineer: collaborate with stakeholders, pin down requirements and document every decision.

decisions.title: Plans and pricing
decisions.context: The first idea was Free, about $20 and about $40 with unlimited use.
decisions.decision: Final plans: Free, Pro at about $5/month and Premium at about $20/month, with a possible $40 Premium+ tier. Free first unlocked Pro access for 30 days, later about 15 days by client decision. Annual billing averages a 17% discount. Pro adds selected tools and custom features; Pro and Premium add PDF watchlist export and share links with configurable access; Premium adds a portfolio dashboard.
decisions.reason: Unlimited use was unsustainable because of computation and server load, and it undercut the product’s value.
decisions.result: One lead registered and tried the app. No paid subscriptions yet, because the application is still incomplete.
decisions.lesson: Price according to value, costs, effort and user needs. Avoid overvaluing or undervaluing the work.

decisions.title: Feature gating
decisions.context: Features included watchlist sharing and export, advanced filters, a portfolio dashboard, automatic refresh, favourites, guided onboarding and monthly Premium reports. Smart email alerts follow each user’s habits, watchlists and marked stocks, and OAuth simplifies sign-in.
decisions.decision: Put the portfolio dashboard and automatic refresh in Premium+. Required registration, with a trial of about 15 days.
decisions.reason: A survey of competitors shaped the split. Unauthorised guest usage raised API and server load, so access had to be restricted.
decisions.lesson: Clarify requirements and feature behaviour early to avoid defects and instability.

decisions.title: Payments approach
decisions.context: Subscription revenue was meant to cover compute and infrastructure and to recognise the development effort.
decisions.decision: Chose Razorpay. Its merchant verification is complete and approved, and it handles currency conversion: about ₹1,800 to ₹1,900 for a $20 plan. Rejected manual bank transfers. PayPal remains a later option.
decisions.reason: Stripe meant a waitlist, request screening and approval timing that did not fit early development in India. Juspay’s fees and limited time ruled it out. Manual bank transfers carried security and scam risks.
decisions.result: No paid subscriptions yet, because development is incomplete. Lovable cloud hosting is now inactive, and the app runs standalone on a Hostinger domain.
decisions.lesson: Handle payment infrastructure and financial information carefully.

decisions.title: Launch
decisions.context: The screener moved from requirements to a public custom domain.
decisions.decision: Launched on a custom domain through Cloudflare, then iterated on branding and logo, SEO and discoverability, speed and a fluid interface.
decisions.reason: A product has to be found and feel fast before anyone stays to use it.
decisions.result: Cloudflare Analytics recorded 17,000+ organic views, primarily from the United States and other regions.
decisions.lesson: Running costs go beyond compute: microservices, paid APIs, infrastructure and development subscriptions all add up.

decisions.title: Traffic
decisions.context: Cloudflare Analytics for equityiq.in, 3 October to 2 November 2026.
decisions.decision: Tracked pageviews, visits, requests and country breakdowns to understand where attention came from.
decisions.reason: Traffic shows reach, and reach has to turn into sustained use.
decisions.lesson: Views alone do not establish sustained product use.
stats: United States 9.11k, France 6.39k, Netherlands 6.19k, Singapore 5.29k, Japan 4.08k

bharat.origin: In 2024, I served as event manager for my college’s E-Cell initiative. We pitched a regional voice-based system to help daily-wage workers with everyday communication and information needs. At NEC E-Summit 2024 at IIT Bombay, I pitched a job-matching app for daily-wage and off-season workers. Our team’s pitch ranked 4th in India. The idea included regional-language support, salary-negotiation help and planned government welfare tie-ups for fair wages.

secret.story: During my cybersecurity internship at Edunet Foundation, I studied bit-level image steganography and built a GUI to hide and retrieve data. This puzzle applies that technique in the browser.
secret.grant: $3,000 is about ₹2,80,000 in India. I would spend about 40 to 50% on a new smartphone, wired earphones and essential accessories. If my Wispr Flow work needs one, I would add a high-end laptop. Otherwise, I would save the remainder toward a better future device.

receipts.title: The Autopsy
receipts.flow: The client initially asked me to build a tool. I approached the requirement differently and developed a complete product end to end: cloud hosting, authentication, multi-user support, administrative access, user and analytics visibility, portfolio dashboards, subscription-based feature restrictions and role- and privilege-based access control. As admin, I could monitor users and application analytics; users reached dashboards and features according to their subscription tier and permissions. The client was satisfied, although I believe there was still room for improvement. The project is a starting point for my freelancing and software development career. Manual development, problem-solving and independent technical understanding will continue to remain valuable.

receipts.title: Voice-First Bharat
receipts.flow: In 2024, I served as an event manager for my college’s E-Cell initiative. During this period, we pitched the idea of developing a regional voice-based system that could assist daily-wage workers with everyday communication and information requirements.

receipts.title: The Secret Layer
receipts.flow: Replace the simple word hunt with a three-image puzzle that teaches the visitor how to uncover the hidden word. Use grayscale or real-world images. The letters must be recoverable through the method explained by the hints, not merely overlaid visibly. Add a concise story that gives context and explains how to begin. Provide progressive hints: a broad observation, the technique to try, then a stronger hint for each image.

receipts.title: Build prompt
receipts.flow: Build a polished, mobile-first, single-page portfolio web app called Out Loud. It should feel memorable, easy to explore, and understandable in about three minutes. Make the design custom and engaging rather than a generic résumé template. Design mobile first, then adapt to larger screens. Use subtle purposeful motion and respect reduced-motion settings.

buildLog:
01 Ideation. Asked for 10 to 15 project ideas that solve real problems, each with problem, solution, existing solutions, gaps and MVP.
02 Simplified plan. Condensed the Out Loud concept and delivery plan into a buildable spec, with a prerequisites and requirements report.
03 First demo. Built the single-page structure: Hero, Autopsy, Voice-First Bharat, Secret Layer, Voice Receipts, Projects and Skills, About and Contact, with marked placeholders and a global animation toggle.
04 Design concepts. Requested three or four small design models before building, then chose one independent visual direction.
05 Refinement. Fixed the title glitch with a typing animation, added dark and light themes, replaced the word hunt with a three-image puzzle and removed carousels and marquees.
06 Private tools. Added the Content Setup tool, Voice Intro recording, print summary and in-browser steganography decoder.
07 Content refresh. Filled sections from the résumés and reference, moved audio and transcripts to a private editor, changed the font and removed promotional labels.
voiceLimit: Automatic corrections can change intended wording, and reviewing a long transcript takes time. Accuracy depends on comfort with pronunciation, intonation, sentence formation and punctuation, and background noise reduces it. Passwords, bank details and confidential messages are unsuitable for dictation.
